title: Rule frontmatter
$comment: Source: agents/reference/docs/frontmatter-contract.md#rules. `type` is authoritative; `alwaysApply` is a Cursor/Cline sidecar and accepted but not enforced.

type.description: `always` = injected verbatim every turn (kernel). `auto` = description stub injected, body loaded on trigger match. `manual` = no auto-injection (zero workspace-budget cost); file remains as a reference document linkable from skills/contexts. Introduced by ADR-004 to demote thin pointer-rules without breaking cross-references.

decision_impact.description: What is at stake when this rule fires — distinct from `type`, which is a DELIVERY class (how the rule reaches the model). `overrides-model-default`: the model's base behaviour is wrong here, so the rule is load-bearing. `encodes-house-choice`: the model would make *a* defensible choice but not *our* choice. `already-complied-with`: the model does this unprompted — the one value that permits removal, and therefore the one carrying an evidence bar (`decision_impact_evidence`, enforced by lint_decision_impact). OPTIONAL by design: classifying all 111 rules in one batch is exactly the shape that trips check_kernel_prefix_stability, so it lands on new rules and on rules touched for another reason.

decision_impact_evidence.description: Required when `decision_impact: already-complied-with`, forbidden otherwise. A pointer a reviewer can follow to the observation that the model complies without this rule — an eval report, a PR discussion, a trajectory sample. The bar exists because that classification is what permits deleting a rule, and 'the model probably does this anyway' is the cheapest possible way to remove a floor that was working precisely because nothing had crossed it.

alwaysApply.description: Optional sidecar for Cursor/Cline; by convention true when type=always, false when type=auto.

items.description: Logical name (preferred — `contexts/<area>/<file>.md`) or project-local (`agents/settings/contexts/<file>.md`). The `.agent-src.uncondensed/` prefix is rejected by the regex; the rewriter (`scripts/condense.py::_rewrite_paths`) resolves logical names at condense time. Rewritten relative forms (`../contexts/...`, `../../contexts/...`) are accepted so the linter passes on the condensed mirror in CI.

load_context.description: Lazy on-demand context references. Use logical names rooted at the source (e.g. `contexts/execution/foo.md`); the `.agent-src.uncondensed/` prefix is forbidden by the regex (road-to-path-fixes.md P5.3). Path rules and budget caps enforced by scripts/lint_load_context.py. Contract: docs/contracts/load-context-schema.md.

load_context_eager.description: Eager auto-loaded context references. Same logical-name rule as `load_context`. Counts against the per-rule char budget; enforced by scripts/lint_load_context.py.

norm.description: The rule's declared NORMATIVE budget, plus where its non-normative remainder went. Optional: a required key would red every existing rule file on the day it lands, which is the gate-that-teaches-you-to-ignore-it failure `src/config/preamble-payload-budget.json` warns about in its own `_comment`. A rule that declares this is asserting that everything left in its body is obligation or routing, and that the rationale a reader may still want is reachable at `remainder`. Measured and enforced by `lint_rule_norm_pin`.

tokens.description: Exact-BPE ceiling (cl100k_base) for the rule body BELOW the frontmatter. Never a chars/4 proxy - this tree ships an exact tokenizer and a pin measured in the other unit would be enforced against a number nobody can reproduce. Derive it from a real measurement of the rule after its remainder has moved out; a pin invented at authoring time is an invented threshold and the lint would then enforce a guess.

remainder.description: Where the prose this rule used to carry now lives - one or more guideline, context, or skill paths. REQUIRED alongside `tokens`, deliberately: a pin with no destination is a licence to delete, and `preservation-guard` forbids deletion during a transformation. The rule must also carry an inbound link to each entry so the relocated prose stays reachable (`check_references`).

tier.description: Hardening tier. Legacy values (1/2a/2b/3/safety-floor/mechanical-already) accepted; new router-canonical values (kernel/tier-1/tier-2) introduced by road-to-kernel-and-router.md Phase 4.

council_depth.description: Optional reasoning-depth marker for AI Council invocations triggered while this rule is active. The only accepted value is 'deep'; omit the key for default depth (setting 'standard' is rejected — every frontmatter byte counts against the context window, and 'standard' is the implicit default). 'deep' instructs the host agent to pass --depth deep to council_cli, which floors rounds at max(ai_council.deep_min_rounds, ai_council.min_rounds). Use for rules that gate architecture, refactoring, or bug-diagnosis flows. See .agent-src.uncondensed/skills/ai-council/SKILL.md.

path_prefix.description: Literal path-prefix match pattern the host evaluates against the file the agent is editing — NOT a file reference. The rewriter leaves it verbatim. Source-of-truth rules that must fire on edits under `.agent-src.uncondensed/` keep that prefix here (the prefix ban applies only to `load_context:` and body links — see road-to-path-fixes.md P2.2 / AI-Council 2026-05-06).

triggers.description: Router activation triggers (Phase 3 of road-to-kernel-and-router.md). Forbidden on kernel rules, required on non-kernel rules. Five match keys: keyword, phrase, file_pattern, path_prefix, command. `intent` was removed — it never auto-matched at runtime and only gave rule authors false confidence that an activation path existed; additionalProperties:false now rejects it. Schema: docs/contracts/rule-router.md.

routes_to.description: Router targets (skill / guideline / command / contract). Forbidden on kernel rules. Non-kernel rules declare either routes_to or self_contained: true. Schema: docs/contracts/rule-router.md.

self_contained.description: Certifies a non-kernel rule whose body IS the constraint — a prohibition, gate, or output-format law with no procedure to delegate — so it legitimately declares no routes_to. May offload detail via load_context. Per-rule certification rationale lives in ADR-210's appendix; the linter errors when a non-kernel rule declares neither routes_to nor this marker. Schema: docs/contracts/rule-router.md.

applies_to_user_types.description: Forward-compatible user-type filter (step-12-universal-os-reframe Phase 4). Rule loads only when the active user-type matches one of these tags. Wired by step-9-user-types-axis once it lands; treated as a no-op gate until then. Free-form tags (e.g. 'support', 'finance', 'recruiting', 'marketing', 'legal-drafting', 'consulting', 'medical-drafting', 'finance-drafting', 'ops', 'analytics-export', 'all') — no enum until the user-types axis closes.

profile.description: Optional profile override; rare. Tier-derived default applies otherwise.

reason.description: Human-readable rationale for the suppression — surfaced in audit logs.

validator_ignore.description: Per-rule allowlist consumed by the post-condensation validator (scripts/check_condensed_paths.py). Rules that document forbidden path substrings as their subject matter (e.g. augment-portability, no-roadmap-references) declare the literal strings here so the gate does not flag itself. road-to-path-fixes.md P5.1.

workspaces.description: ADR-013 workspace ids (additive discovery axis). Closed vocabulary enforced by scripts/lint_artefact_frontmatter.py against config/discovery/workspaces.yml.

packs.description: ADR-013 pack ids (additive discovery axis). Closed vocabulary enforced by scripts/lint_artefact_frontmatter.py against config/discovery/packs.yml.

roles.description: Subagent role-mode scoping axis (road-to-lean-agent-init Phase 4), parallel to `workspaces`/`packs`. Closed vocabulary — the six RoleMode ids from src/scripts/_lib/subagent_spawn.ts. Absent/empty = untagged, fails safe (ships to every role). Kernel rules (type: always) always ship regardless of this field. Enforced via this schema's `enum` (not a src/config/discovery/*.yml + lint_artefact_frontmatter.ts cross-check like workspaces/packs) because lint_artefact_frontmatter.ts still scans the retired legacy rules tree (0 artifacts post-ADR-051 src/ migration) and is a no-op for src/rules/*.md today; validate_frontmatter.ts (the active src/rules linter) enforces this enum instead.

enforced_by.description: What mechanically enforces this rule. `validator:<script>` and `test:<path>` must resolve on disk AND be wired into a taskfile, workflow, or the hook manifest — a script that exists but runs nowhere resolves to unwired, not covered. `hook:<name>` must be registered in hook_manifest.yaml with fail_closed: true; a hook that never blocks is `observer:`, not `validator:`. `instruction-only: <reason>` declares an honestly model-carried obligation and is counted as a recorded gap — the reason is MANDATORY in the pattern, because a bare marker is a claim with no triage record behind it and resolves to `missing`, which the --check ratchet reds on. The bare `none` spelling it replaces stays legal for exactly one reason: `non-destructive-by-default` still carries it and is a kernel rule that block_kernel_rule_writes denies agent writes to, so retiring the value outright would make a CI-green tree unreachable for any agent. Resolved, not trusted, by check_enforcement_coverage.ts.

obligation_frequency.description: How often this rule's obligation comes due — the question `enforced_by` does not answer. `enforced_by` asks *does something carry this*; a carrier can be wired, reachable and firing and still fire in the wrong slot (session-canary: a per-task obligation carried by a session_start hook, measured dropped on ~13 of 15 task starts while counting as enforced). Joined against the carrier's per-slot-and-platform firing frequency by check_enforcement_coverage.ts. The value set is a FOREST, not a chain — three roots that never cover one another: lifecycle (`per-turn` > `per-task` > `per-session`), repository-write (`per-commit`, `per-file-write`), and external-event (`per-event`). `per-edit` is a fourth, incomparable-to-`per-turn` case: pre/post_tool_use fire per tool call, so a conversational turn with no tool call fires them zero times. `none` = no recurring obligation (a pointer or reference rule). Required on every non-kernel rule by validate_frontmatter.ts; the nine kernel rules are exempt because block_kernel_rule_writes.ts denies agent writes to them, and that exemption is derived from _lib/kernel_rules.ts so it closes itself the moment a rule leaves the kernel.

trust.description: ADR-013 trust block. Vocabulary mirrored by scripts/lint_artefact_frontmatter.py.

composition_review.description: The authoring-search record (road-to-composition-before-creation Phase 3): which incumbents were searched before this artifact was created, and the declared delta for each. Optional on existing artifacts by design — nothing is backfilled. Distinct from `collision_ok`, which is keyed by trigger VALUE and fires only on a trigger collision; this is keyed by INCUMBENT and is written at authoring time whether or not any trigger is shared.

candidate.description: The incumbent searched, as `skill:<name>` / `rule:<name>` / `command:<name>` / `guideline:<path>`. The literal `none` records a search that found no credible incumbent — the value that must exist so an author is never pushed to invent one to satisfy the schema.

disposition.description: What happened to this candidate. `create_separate` is the value no other disposition vocabulary in this tree can express: an incumbent exists, was evaluated, and a separate artifact was authored anyway.

rationale.description: One sentence naming the delta — what this artifact does that the candidate does not, or why the candidate could not absorb it. A lint checks that this is non-empty and that `candidate` resolves; it cannot check that the search was diligent, and does not pretend to.

collision_ok.description: Per-trigger collision disposition: maps a trigger VALUE (case-insensitive) shared with >=1 other rule to a one-line reason why this rule also firing on it is correct. Enforced by scripts/lint_trigger_collisions.ts.

precedence.description: Alternative collision disposition: maps a shared trigger VALUE to an integer ordering; a collision is clean when ALL sharers declare pairwise-distinct integers for it. Enforced by scripts/lint_trigger_collisions.ts.

install.description: ADR-013 install hints (default-on at consumer install; user-removable).
